privacy_rounding: $10 increment rounding enforced across all model outputs

paths_comparison.name: Path 1A (Pure): Same-Year Sale & Lump-Sum Reinvestment
paths_comparison.prop_a_action: Sell in same tax year as inheritance (IRC §1014 full step-up, $0 cap gains)
paths_comparison.prop_b_action: Remain in Unit 3 as primary residence; keep Units 1 & 2 rented ($7,150/mo base)
paths_comparison.reinvestment_risk: High entry sequence risk if inherited at market peak (mitigated by Path 1B)

paths_comparison.name: Path 1B (Mixed): Same-Year Sale + 24–36m 3M–2Y Treasury Ladder -> Equities
paths_comparison.prop_a_action: Sell in same tax year; park 100% in CA-tax-exempt 3M–2Y Treasuries, phase into stocks over 30 mos
paths_comparison.prop_b_action: Remain in Unit 3 as primary residence; keep Units 1 & 2 rented
paths_comparison.reinvestment_risk: Low — Softens 1929/2008 crash entry drawdown by +24% to +38%

paths_comparison.name: Path 4 (Mixed): Occupy Property A for 3 Yrs (Prop 19 + IRC §121), Then Sell
paths_comparison.prop_a_action: Move in within 1 yr (BOE-19-P), occupy 3 yrs, claim $500k IRC §121 exclusion, then sell
paths_comparison.prop_b_action: Rent Unit 3 during 3-yr Cupertino stay (or hold vacant), then return or reallocate
paths_comparison.reinvestment_risk: Moderate — Delays equity entry by 3 yrs; exposes to 3 yrs of Prop 19 partial tax

paths_comparison.name: Path 3 (Pure): Occupy Property A Long-Term (Claim Prop 19 Exclusion)
paths_comparison.prop_a_action: Move into Cupertino permanently within 1 yr; file BOE-19-P to cap reassessment at FBYV + $1M adj.
paths_comparison.prop_b_action: Rent out vacated SF Unit 3 (~$3,500/mo in 2026$) alongside Units 1 & 2
paths_comparison.reinvestment_risk: Low market timing risk, but high geographic & seismic concentration risk

paths_comparison.name: Path 5B (Mixed): Rent Property A for 7 Yrs, Then IRC §1031 Like-Kind Exchange
paths_comparison.prop_a_action: Rent for 7 yrs (full Prop 19 reassessment), claim 27.5-yr depreciation, then 1031 exchange into DST/multifamily
paths_comparison.prop_b_action: Remain in Unit 3 as primary residence; keep Units 1 & 2 rented
paths_comparison.liquidity_score: Low (Illiquid Real Estate / DST + FTB Form 3840 tracking)
paths_comparison.reinvestment_risk: Moderate — Suffers 7 yrs of low Cupertino gross yield (~2.2%) & full Prop 19 tax reset

paths_comparison.name: Path 2 (Pure): Rent Out Property A Long-Term (Full Prop 19 Reassessment)
paths_comparison.prop_a_action: Hold as single-family rental; loses Prop 19 exclusion (100% reassessed to FMV)
paths_comparison.prop_b_action: Remain in Unit 3 as primary residence; keep Units 1 & 2 rented
paths_comparison.reinvestment_risk: Severe Yield Compression — Full Prop 19 tax eats ~45%–55% of gross Cupertino rent

black_swan_regimes.name: 1929–1939 Great Depression & Deflationary Crash
black_swan_regimes.historical_basis: S&P 500 -86% peak-to-trough (1929–1932), CPI -24% deflation, 3M–2Y Treasuries +3.5% to +1.5% positive nominal/real yield

black_swan_regimes.name: 2008–2013 Global Financial Crisis & Housing De-leveraging
black_swan_regimes.historical_basis: S&P 500 -37.0% in Year 1 (-56.8% peak-to-trough), Bay Area RE -18% to -27%, 2Y Treasury rally +4.2% to +1.8% flight-to-safety

black_swan_regimes.name: 2000–2009 Silicon Valley Dot-Com Bust & Lost Decade
black_swan_regimes.historical_basis: NASDAQ -78% / S&P 500 3 consecutive down years (-9.1%, -11.9%, -22.1%), Santa Clara County rental concessions -15% to -20%

black_swan_regimes.name: 1973–1982 Stagflation & Volcker Interest Rate Shock
black_swan_regimes.historical_basis: S&P 500 -14.7% and -26.5% in 1973–74 while CPI hit 11%–13.5%; 3M–2Y Treasury yields rose to 9%–15%; CA Prop 13 passed 1978

black_swan_regimes.name: Bay Area M7.0 Hayward/San Andreas Quake + Tech Concentration Shock
black_swan_regimes.historical_basis: Localized 25%–35% structural damage if uninsured for earthquake (CEA 15% deductible), 18-month uninhabitability, diversified global portfolio unaffected
